newsitem.title: UK: Britain gives India $78 million to eradicate polio.
newsitem.headline: Britain gives India $78 million to eradicate polio.

text.p: Britain is contributing 47.5 million pounds ($78 million) to a vaccination scheme in India to try to eradicate polio worldwide by the year 2000, the government said on Monday.
In India, which has a population of 920 million people, there were 2,993 cases of polio last year -- more than those in the rest of the world combined.

"The programme aims to strike a body blow against the disease once and for all. If we can eliminate it in India, then the rest of the world will follow," Baroness Lynda Chalker, minister for overseas development, said in a statement.

The Pulse Polio Programme is expected to cost 139 million pounds over three years. In addition to Britain's contribution, other donors are expected to provide up to 55 million pounds and the Indian government will make up the shortfall.
Polio, an infectious disease involving the spinal cord and the brain, usually affects children and can result in paralysis.

If the programme is successful polio will be the second virus, after smallpox, to be completely eradicated. According to the World Health Organisation, there were 2,836 cases in 1995 around the world, excluding India. The only countries where data was not available were Gabon, Afghanistan and Somalia. ($1=.6107 Pound)
